narr: High pressure situated south of the International Border led to a westerly flow aloft, which caused dry air advection. However, there was still sufficient moisture (PWAT around 1.5 inches) and instability (MLCAPE 1000-2000 J/KG) as well as a subtle disturbance in the upper-levels to result in the development of strong thunderstorms across portions of south-central and southwest Arizona. Downdraft CAPE values were also in excess of 1500 J/KG, which led to favorable conditions for some of these thunderstorms to produce severe wind gusts.
ev: Video of flash flooding on Peralta Road, east of Gold Canyon, which stranded motorists. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

A Flood Control District of Maricopa County Stream Gauge of Jackrabbit Wash at Vulture Mine Road reported water levels rising rapidly above alarm stage at around 1713 MST, with a peak flow of 4.88 feet (3651 cfs) at 1803 MST, and going back down below alarm stage at around 1926 MST. This amount of water flow likely flooded Aguila Road upstream of the gauge and Wickenburg Road, where a water rescue was performed, located 5 miles downstream of the gauge. No injuries were reported. Based on the report from the Phoenix Dispatch, water got halfway up on an unoccupied vehicle stuck along the flood waters from Jackrabbit Wash located along Wickenburg Road.
